data.summary: The pod startup is slow, taking 33.0 seconds to become Ready, which breaches the 10.0-second SLO. This is primarily due to the application spending 25.648 seconds downloading a 262 MB model. The model is downloaded on every cold start because the MODEL_DIR is configured on an emptyDir volume, preventing persistence across pod restarts.

findings.statement: The pod startup took 33.0 seconds to become Ready, exceeding the 10.0-second SLO.
The 'model.download' span within the 'app_init' phase took 25.648 seconds, contributing significantly to the overall startup time.
A 262144000 byte (262 MB) model was downloaded during startup, as indicated by the 'model.download' span attributes.
The 'model.download' operation reported 'cache_hit: false', confirming the model was fetched remotely rather than from a local cache.
The 'MODEL_DIR' is mounted on an 'emptyDir' volume named 'work', which does not persist data across pod restarts, necessitating repeated model downloads.

ruled_out.reason: The image pull duration was 4.921 seconds for 53328919 bytes, which is not the primary contributor to the 33.0-second startup time.
The scheduling phase duration was 0.0 seconds, and there were no failed scheduling events.
The readiness probe duration was 0.0 seconds, and there were no probe failures after the application was ready.

recommendations.rationale: Keep model weights on a persistent volume, pre-populated by a prefetch job, and enable the application's cache reuse. This will allow subsequent starts to load the model from local disk, avoiding repeated downloads.
